analysis.title: October pause followed by December hike
key_insights: SEB expects the Fed to hold the policy rate at 3.75-4.00% at the 27-28 October FOMC. Markets price over 90% probability of no change.
SEB's base case is one more 25 bp hike in December, then cuts by end-2027 and two more in the first half of 2028 toward a neutral rate of about 3.25-3.50%.

The Fed raised rates by 25 bps on 15-16 September, the first hike since July 2023. Chair Warsh repeated hawkish views from his Jackson Hole speech, and markets then priced about 50% odds of an October hike.
Calls for a pause from Williams, Jefferson and Waller, plus Warsh's silence on policy at the IMF event on 16 October, moved market pricing to a pause. Markets read Warsh's restraint as dovish.
SEB expects Hammack and Logan to dissent in favour of a hike in October. Warsh is thought to prefer a unanimous vote when raising rates.

With no change and no new projections, the meeting's focus is the degree of consensus, any statement changes, and whether Warsh repeats his hawkish language at the press conference. SEB expects no clear signals.

The Fed has mostly avoided rate changes in the weeks before federal elections. CME Group found no change between 1 October and election day before two thirds of federal elections since 1972. The midterms are on 3 November.

Core PCE for August was revised down by 0.4 percentage points, more than expected, and employment growth slowed markedly in August. Labour supply is also slowing, so the Fed is unlikely to worry about labour market downside.
Core PCE still ran at 3% y/y in August. September CPI came in above expectations and PPI price pressures are rising. SEB sees a possible slight acceleration in core PCE in the 29 October release.
Falling equity prices could tighten financial conditions. Real yields are back near their level at the September decision, so yields are less of a concern than before.
In the September minutes, all FOMC members backed the hike but differed on why. Many saw it as insurance against sticky inflation, while others saw it as required by their own inflation outlook.
In the September projections, 16 of 18 participants expected at least one more hike this year, and 8 of 18 expected two more hikes by end-2026 or end-2027.

Energy prices are the main upside risk. Persistently high prices with no end to the Middle East conflict could tip the Fed toward a third hike in early 2027. Falling equity and debt markets and higher mortgage rates could prolong the pause.

Markets priced another 100 bps of hikes through end-2027 in late September. They now price a little over 2.5 hikes, with the next in December, which SEB calls still somewhat aggressive versus its forecast.
A Warsh task force will hold a hearing in San Francisco on 16 November on productivity and the labour market.

risk_factors: Persistently high energy prices from the Middle East conflict could spread to other prices and tip the Fed toward a third hike in early 2027.
Strong demand from the AI build-out and resilient households could let companies pass energy costs on to customers.
Falling equity and debt markets and rising household mortgage rates could prolong the pause.
Falling equity prices could tighten financial conditions beyond what the Fed intends.
A surprise tightening in October would upset markets, which SEB regards as unlikely.
Hawkish dissents from Hammack and Logan are possible.
vol_and_positioning: Markets priced about 50% odds of an October hike after the September meeting. They now price over 90% odds of a hold.
Markets priced a full 100 bps of further hikes through end-2027 in late September and now price a little over 2.5 hikes.
geopolitical: The conflict in the Middle East has pushed oil prices higher and is an upside risk to inflation and to the rate path.
SEB cites tariffs and energy prices as successive shocks to inflation.

tension_points.bull_case: Persistently high energy prices, strong AI-driven demand and resilient households could let firms pass on costs, pushing the Fed toward a third hike in early 2027. Hammack and Logan favour moving rates to a restrictive level quickly.
tension_points.bear_case: Falling equity and debt markets, higher mortgage rates and softer data such as the downward core PCE revision and slower retail sales could prolong the pause. Williams, Jefferson and Waller have signalled no urgency to hike again.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Continued market unrest with falling equity and debt markets and rising mortgage rates would prolong the pause, while persistently high energy prices with no end to the Middle East conflict would favour a third hike in early 2027.

theme_stances.key_argument: The Fed is expected to hold in October because of the proximity of the midterm elections, mixed data and tighter financial conditions, and softer signals from Fed members.
theme_stances.evidence: in line with our long-held forecast

theme_stances.key_argument: SEB stays with one more hike in December because it sees the inflation shocks as temporary.
theme_stances.evidence: We stick to our view that the Fed will deliver one more rate increase
